subject: Novamed capacity commitment — staggered commit phases & checklist
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita@novamed.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@novamed.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Novamed capacity planning — next steps

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re excited: the primary ask from our infra and ML teams is a clear, phased plan showing how Redwood would support our production rollout for clinical embeddings and a low-latency chat assistant. Key questions for the MAP: lead times for Dedicated vs Private deployments, recommended GPU pool sizing for steady-state vs peak, and a procurement checklist we can share with Finance.

High level: target go-live in Q4 but want an initial evaluation window in Sept. Estimated peak: 120 embed QPS and ~1,000 chat tokens/s during batch periods (rough ballpark). We’d like a staggered commitment option — be able to commit to a baseline capacity and add tranches after successful evaluation gates.

Attached: Novamed_RFP_specs.pdf (high level throughput SLAs and data residency notes). Can you start a MAP draft that includes milestone gating (eval -> PO -> provisioning)? Also include typical SLA implications for Dedicated vs Private.

Thanks,
Anita Rao
Director, ML Platforms
Novamed Health

Attachments: Novamed_RFP_specs.pdf (pdf)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Rao <anita@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novamed capacity planning — next steps

Anita —

Appreciate the context and the RFP. I’ve looped in Ben (infra product) and Laura (sales ops) to help shape a staged MAP. High level proposal we’ll put in writing:

- Phase A (Evaluation, 4–6 weeks): sandbox endpoints + 2–4 nodes mimicking production traffic; performance gates (latency p50/p95, model quality checks on your eval set).
- Phase B (Pilot, 8 weeks): staggered commit — baseline capacity (sized for 30–40% of peak) with option to add tranche 1 at PO.
- Phase C (Full prod): full GPU pool provisioning and network configs + runbook handover.

Immediate asks from our side: a short worksheet with peak concurrency and expected batch patterns so Ben can size the pool. We’ll draft a MAP v1 and share a procurement checklist (PO, billing lead time, on-prem rack requirements if Private).

I attached a starter: Draft_MAP_Novamed_v1.pdf. Laura will follow up with timeline constraints and procurement language.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Novamed capacity planning — next steps

Anita/Jordan —

Quick technical sizing notes (based on the numbers you shared):

1) Baseline profile (evaluation/pilot):
  - Embeddings: 120 qps peak -> recommended baseline pool: 4x A100-40GB (or 6x A30 equivalent with quantized model path).
  - Chat (low-latency): 100 concurrent users -> 6x A100-40GB for steady inference with continuous batching disabled during low-latency windows.

2) Peak profile (full prod):
  - To cover headroom and burst (120 qps + batch spikes) -> target pool: 8–10x A100-40GB. Quantized 4-bit variants can reduce effective GPU needs ~1.6x but will require quality gating during eval.

3) Lead times and procurement considerations:
  - Redwood Dedicated (hosted/reserved pools): operationally available in ~4–8 weeks if capacity is available in the region; if we need committed hardware procurement for a tranche, plan 8–12 weeks for allocation/validation.
  - Redwood Private (customer VPC/on-prem): typical lead time 12–20 weeks depending on rack availability, networking coordination, and KMS integration. On-prem may require a site readiness assessment (+2–3 weeks).

4) Staggered-commit recommendation:
  - Tranche 0 (evaluation): 2–4 nodes on a shared eval pool.
  - Tranche 1 (baseline commit): 30–40% of estimated steady-state pool with 4-week payback window for scale testing.
  - Tranche 2 (scale to prod): ramp to target pool over 6–8 weeks after successful gating.

I’m attaching a quick capacity worksheet that maps workload patterns to pool sizes. If you can send actual daily RPS / token counts for a representative week, I’ll run a more precise sizing.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Capacity_Specs_Table.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Anita Rao <anita@novamed.com>

Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novamed capacity planning — next steps

Thanks Ben — useful breakdown. A few clarifications from infra/ML:

- Workloads: embeddings will mostly run as near-real-time batch jobs (peaks up to 120 qps for 10–15 minute windows). Chat will be interactive but low concurrency outside business hours.
- We can commit to a baseline tranche (Tranche 1) if the evaluation shows <=5% quality degradation for quantized variants.
- Procurement: we prefer a staged PO where we issue an initial PO for Tranche 1 with an option to increase spend under the same contract. Can you include sample contract language or PO wording?

Also, can you provide rough cost delta between Dedicated vs Private for the same pool size (ballpark per-month)? That will determine which route we prefer.

—Anita

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Draft MAP & milestone checklist (Novamed)

Hi Anita —

Attached is a cleaned up MAP v2 that reflects the staggered-commit approach and includes procurement language for a phased PO. Highlights:

- Evaluation window (4 weeks): test harness, model quality gates (we will run evals using your prompt suite), performance SLOs.
- Acceptance criteria to trigger Tranche 1: latency p95 < 350ms (chat) and cosine similarity delta < 0.05 on embeddings.
- Procurement checklist: PO -> Billing team onboarding -> SSO + KMS approvals -> Provisioning window (Reserved Dedicated: 6–10 weeks; Private: 12–18 weeks).
- Canary/rollout plan: Canary for 2 weeks on 25% traffic then 50% then full.

DocuSign and scope: we’ve provisioned a DocuSign envelope (link below) for the base MSA + SOW. If you want staged POs, we can add amendment language so you don’t need a fully new contract for each tranche.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/novamed-map-ds
